findings.text: 已有合法本地Stata和定量能力者，在匿名副本中让宿主Agent运行/核查do任务；需求频率/收益待独立对照，见[Q01](#research-q01)。
CLI真实注册profile工具→MCP/guard→来源快照→本地Stata进程→日志/审计返回；metadata经Python handler，宿主负责模型决策，见[Q01](#research-q01)至[Q03](#research-q03)。

工程统计只有Markdown列项，未计核心Python，不等代码量/原创量或工时，不手补PY数量。四材料摘要/固定SOURCE身份已核，无正式identity旧稿。检查分发CLI到MCP/默认同步Unix执行、async代表、guard/安装/metadata真实callee与快照审计validator、局部资源退出；未执行目标/脚本/测试或外部调用，未全审Stata语法/ado闭包、Windows所有分支、全部API/宿主审批、并发与数据脱敏。
Python包1.25.2，含MCP/CLI/API与独立Skill版本；无npm对象版本，不把外部Stata/ado和远端安装统一。固定提交日期非发布日期。
Python/MCP与可写资料；本地Stata许可用于真实统计执行，非所有元数据一概必需；模型/平台按功能，四列表见[Q04](#research-q04)。
已有许可用户也需固定路径/权限、记录来源/环境；持续模型/统计/证据资源，失败先查partial状态，退出保存研究工件；现金/人工四阶段见[Q04](#research-q04)。
已有合法Stata与方法能力，匿名本地副本、不用unsafe安装；确认guard、目录、资源/timeout实际配置，按已知答案核结果再扩大，见[Q04](#research-q04)、[Q05](#research-q05)。
来源可追、真实执行与证据可校验能减少手工串接，但语义/方法与净节时未证；三项效果表见[Q02](#research-q02)。
分清MCP真实caller与API/CLI边界；现有快照/run_id/fullSHA与guard值得保留，安装确认bool、资源默认、进程/研究终态不混同。
标准接口、路径/命令检查、真执行快照与审计链接便于结果追查；独立操作见主能力表，现有审计不等研究正确，见[Q02](#research-q02)。
MCP安装ctx审批停用/API自动confirm与Skill逐次询问不一致；数据边界/URLguard及RAM监视并非默认全开，进程成功/日志/全hash不等研究成立，见[Q02](#research-q02)至[Q04](#research-q04)。
超出现有do快照/审计，检验单次实证任务的数据/环境/规格和预设结果断言绑定；基线/指标/停止条件见[Q05](#research-q05)。

technical.rationale: [Q01](#research-q01)标准MCP到已有Stata组合novelty25%超纯文档0%，非新统计算法阻50%；[Q02](#research-q02)快照真实执行/审计与[Q03](#research-q03)guard机制50%超裸命令桥25%，审批说明/当前callee与完整边界未闭合阻75%；标准MCP+CLI/API/Skill的transfer50%超单UI25%，Stata/平台/依赖兼容未运行阻75%；日志/证据串接simplification50%超手贴25%，方法验收/维护工时未证阻75%。

business.rationale: [Q01](#research-q01)/[Q02](#research-q02)运行到审计workflow50%超单帮助25%，研究成果正确/真实用户对照阻75%；标准接口+CLI/Skill交付delivery/reach50%超只本机模块25%，平台/客户端和发布物未验证阻75%；[Q04](#research-q04)可选RAM kill/timeout/async并发上界给资源控制economics25%超无机制0%，默认monitor关且非全局硬隔离、无总费用收益实测阻50%。

recommendation.reason: 已有合法本地Stata和定量研究能力的人员，可在匿名数据副本中用 MCP-for-Stata 让宿主Agent运行已审do文件、读取日志并保留来源证据。相比手贴命令和手工找日志，源码支持真实Stata执行、快照与审计链接，但工具说明中的逐次安装确认不等当前服务器行为，执行结束也不能代替样本、规格和研究结果验收。若目录或数据范围不明、安装缺可信授权、日志或输出不符预设答案，应暂停后续执行和重试，保留快照/日志及真实数据差异，退回原有Stata与人工方法检查流程。

data.reports:
# MCP-for-Stata > 让宿主Agent调用本地Stata与数据/日志工具，保存来源快照和执行审计；默认保护、真实安装确认与研究结果验收须分别核查。 ## 研究范围 - **仓库**：[SepineTam/mcp-for-stata](https://github.com/SepineTam/mcp-for-stata) - **版本号**：1.25.2（Python项目声明；Stata/ado/Skill各有版本）（[固定提交 1e94c3bfe82675eed8c85b18f6c9303dd92b4757](https://github.com/SepineTam/mcp-for-stata/tree/1e94c3bfe82675eed8c85b18f6c9303dd92b4757)） - **版本日期**：2026-10-19（固定提交日期，北京时间；不是包发布日期） ## 结论状态 固定源闭合分发CLI注册、MCP do到真实Unix子进程/执行快照/日志和审计校验；核异步/平台开关、关键guard/元数据与安装callee。未运行目标/付费Stata/模型或验证统计结果；限已有许可研究者匿名副本试用。 ## 洞察短评 - **用途**：已有合法本地Stata和定量能力者，在匿名副本中让宿主Agent运行/核查do任务；需求频率/收益待独立对照，见[Q01](#research-q01)。 - **亮点**：标准接口、路径/命令检查、真执行快照与审计链接便于结果追查；独立操作见主能力表，现有审计不等研究正确，见[Q02](#research-q02)。 - **思考**：MCP安装ctx审批停用/API自动confirm与Skill逐次询问不一致；数据边界/URLguard及RAM监视并非默认全开，进程成功/日志/全hash不等研究成立，见[Q02](#research-q02)至[Q04](#research-q04)。 - **建议**：超出现有do快照/审计，检验单次实证任务的数据/环境/规格和预设结果断言绑定；基线/指标/停止条件见[Q05](#research-q05)。 采用建议：已有合法Stata与方法能力，匿名本地副本、不用unsafe安装；确认guard、目录、资源/timeout实际配置，按已知答案核结果再扩大，见[Q04](#research-q04)、[Q05](#research-q05)。 ## 核心贡献 标准接口、路径/命令检查、真执行快照与审计链接便于结果追查；独立操作见主能力表，现有审计不等研究正确，见[Q02](#research-q02)。 ## 关键质疑 MCP安装ctx审批停用/API自动confirm与Skill逐次询问不一致；数据边界/URLguard及RAM监视并非默认全开，进程成功/日志/全hash不等研究成立，见[Q02](#research-q02)至[Q04](#research-q04)。 ## 重点创新推演与最小验证 超出现有do快照/审计，检验单次实证任务的数据/环境/规格和预设结果断言绑定；基线/指标/停止条件见[Q05](#research-q05)。 受控合法Stata匿名已知答案任务，对照普通日志和当前审计；核guard开关/安装真实同意、资源/部分输出、数据/规格变更与误判，见[Q05](#research-q05)。 ## 场景与替代办法 已有合法本地Stata和定量能力者，在匿名副本中让宿主Agent运行/核查do任务；需求频率/收益待独立对照，见[Q01](#research-q01)。 手工Stata/编辑器/日志与已有MCP工具宿主；不把Stata引擎、模型和统计识别当本项目新算法。 ## 依赖与流程 Python/MCP与可写资料；本地Stata许可用于真实统计执行，非所有元数据一概必需；模型/平台按功能，四列表见[Q04](#research-q04)。 宿主发现当前工具→准备匿名数据/do→检查/快照/执行→读日志/审计→人核规格/结果；完整步骤见[Q01](#research-q01)。 ## 成本与效果 已有许可用户也需固定路径/权限、记录来源/环境；持续模型/统计/证据资源，失败先查partial状态，退出保存研究工件；现金/人工四阶段见[Q04](#research-q04)。 来源可追、真实执行与证据可校验能减少手工串接，但语义/方法与净节时未证；三项效果表见[Q02](#research-q02)。 ## 研究问题与完整回答 **插件研究总目标**：固定源码核真实MCP执行/返回、guard/审计/资源边界及实证任务采用方向。 ### Q01 · 真实入口、对象及相对手动Stata的贡献是什么？ **研究主题**：场景与需求、功能与机制、贡献与相对优势 #### 完整回答 这是Python MCP server/CLI/API配Skills的外部工具工程，真实entry_type为tool，不是根DSH bundle或自带通用模型循环。pyproject声明stata-mcp 1.25.2、Python>=3.11，console script到stata_mcp.cli.main；CLI server分支实际handle_server→选core/all/unsafe→register_tools→MCPServer.run，默认all，不把root main.py仅run当工具已挂载的证明。MCPServer实例带AuditMiddleware，注册函数按profile、平台和工具开关过滤，再server.tool装函数。get_data_info在Windows MCP默认隐藏，help仅Unix，ado安装只unsafe，故不能从源码函数存在推各客户端同时有所有工具。 已有本地Stata与定量方法能力的研究人员，可让宿主Agent写/运行do文件、取数据描述/日志/帮助，并保存执行证据。相对在GUI手贴命令/找日志，增量是标准工具接口、路径/命令guard、受控执行与来源快照/审计链接；Stata统计引擎、模型选择/决策和研究识别不由此项目重新实现。包的Skills给导出/回归默认与审计流程，是操作指引，不能当统计结论已经核验。主能力按独立操作列在主表。 | 步骤 | 执行者与动作 | 判据/失败 | |---|---|---| | 连接 | 宿主启动CLI server并发现当前profile工具 | 核实际工具清单/平台限制，不把连接成功当执行成功 | | 准备 | 用户/宿主Agent检查数据、写do文件 | Python API可写文件；不是MCP自动完成研究设计 | | 运行 | 工具先路径/命令检查，再StataDo执行来源快照 | 拒绝/超时/进程错误与结果路径分别看 | | 读取 | 取日志、可选错误内容/元数据 | logpath/returncode不等分析正确 | | 验收 | 研究者核样本/模型/输出与研究任务 | 审计完整性和研究正确性分开 | #### 证据与依据 **依据 1 · 源码核查**：[pyproject.toml:1-10](https://github.com/SepineTam/mcp-for-stata/blob/1e94c3bfe82675eed8c85b18f6c9303dd92b4757/pyproject.toml#L1-L10) Python对象/1.25.2/要求与许可声明。
查看原文（10行） ```text [project] name = "stata-mcp" version = "1.25.2" description = "MCP-for-Stata: a stable, security-first MCP server and CLI for integrating local Stata into Claude Code, Codex, OpenClaw, and other AI research workflows." readme = "README.md" authors = [ { name = "Song Tan", email = "sepinetam@gmail.com" } ] requires-python = ">=3.11" license = { text = "AGPL-3.0" } ```
**依据 2 · 源码核查**：[pyproject.toml:48-65](https://github.com/SepineTam/mcp-for-stata/blob/1e94c3bfe82675eed8c85b18f6c9303dd92b4757/pyproject.toml#L48-L65) 依赖与真实CLI console入口。
查看原文（18行） ```text dependencies = [ "installed-apps-scanner>=0.1.0,<0.2; sys_platform == 'darwin'", "winapps>=0.2.0,<0.3; sys_platform == 'win32'", "mcp[cli]>=2.1.1,<3.0", "opentelemetry-sdk>=1.44.0,<2.0", "cryptography>=50.0.0", "pandas>=3.0.0,<4.0.0", "pexpect>=4.9.0", "openpyxl>=3.1.5", "psutil>=7.2.2", "pyreadstat>=1.3.4", "requests>=2.34.0", "tomli-w>=1.2.0", ] [project.scripts] stata-mcp = "stata_mcp.cli:main" ```
**依据 3 · 源码核查**：[src/stata_mcp/cli/_cli.py:69-91](https://github.com/SepineTam/mcp-for-stata/blob/1e94c3bfe82675eed8c85b18f6c9303dd92b4757/src/stata_mcp/cli/_cli.py#L69-L91) 正常server/default分支实际调用handle_server。
查看原文（23行） ```text if args.command == "discover": sys.exit(handle_discover(args)) if args.command == "server": handle_server(args) return if args.command == "config": exit_code = handle_config(args) if exit_code == 2: config_parser.print_help() sys.exit(exit_code) if args.command == "install": sys.exit(handle_install(args)) if args.command == "update": sys.exit(handle_update(args)) if args.command == "verify": sys.exit(handle_verify(args)) handle_server(args) ```

      "path": "README.md",
      "content": "<div align=\"center\">\n  <a href=\"https://aidea-labs.com/open/projects/mcp-for-stata\">\n    <img src=\"assets/mcp-for-stata-stata-ai-data-analysis.jpg\" alt=\"MCP-for-Stata (Stata-MCP): let Claude Code, Codex, and other AI agents run local Stata for regression analysis and empirical research\" width=\"300\"/>\n  </a>\n</div>\n\n# MCP-for-Stata (Stata-MCP): Run Stata with ANY Agent\n\nMCP-for-Stata is an safety first open-source MCP server and CLI tool with Skills lets any AI agent you use invoke local Stata on your device for regression analysis, econometrics, paper replication, and empirical research. It provides command guards, resource monitoring, automatic log capture, and cross-platform client installation, while you retain control of your data and Stata license.\n\nTurn Claude Code, Codex, and other AI agents into an on-demand research assistant.\n\n> Stata is a registered trademark of StataCorp LLC. This project is an independent community-developed tool and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by StataCorp LLC.\n\n[![en](https://img.shields.io/badge/lang-English-red.svg)](README.md)\n[![cn](https://img.shields.io/badge/语言-中文-yellow.svg)](README.zh-CN.md)\n[![fr](https://img.shields.io/badge/langue-Français-blue.svg)](README.fr.md)\n[![es](https://img.shields.io/badge/idioma-Español-green.svg)](README.es.md)\n[![Publish to PyPI](https://github.com/SepineTam/mcp-for-stata/actions/workflows/python-package.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/SepineTam/mcp-for-stata/actions/workflows/python-package.yml)\n[![PyPI version](https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/stata-mcp.svg)](https://pypi.org/project/stata-mcp/)\n[![PyPI Downloads](https://static.pepy.tech/badge/stata-mcp)](https://pepy.tech/projects/stata-mcp)\n[![License: AGPL 3.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-AGPL%203.0-blue.svg)](LICENSE)\n[![OpenSSF Best Practices](https://www.bestpractices.dev/projects/14255/badge)](https://www.bestpractices.dev/projects/14255)\n[![Issue](https://img.shields.io/badge/Issue-report-green.svg)](https://github.com/sepinetam/mcp-for-stata/issues/new)\n[![Ask DeepWiki](https://deepwiki.com/badge.svg)](https://deepwiki.com/SepineTam/mcp-for-stata)\n\n<!-- mcp-name: io.github.SepineTam/stata-mcp -->\n\n---\n## 💡 Quick Start\n\nYou do not need to edit any configuration. Just tell your agent:\n\n```text\nInstall MCP-for-Stata for yourself globally following the instructions in the GitHub repository at SepineTam/mcp-for-stata.\n```\n\n## 🆕 News\n- 📖 **Skills installed by default**: Stata-related skills are now installed together with the MCP, no separate setup needed. Inspect the repository before installation.\n    \"\"\"\n    config = Config(config_file=config_file)\n    package, source, package_source_from = validate_ado_install_request(\n        package,\n        source,\n        package_source_from,\n        allowed_github_repositories=(\n            config.ADO_INSTALL_ALLOWED_GITHUB_REPOSITORIES\n        ),\n    )\n    runtime = create_runtime_context(config_file=config_file, require_stata=True)\n\n    logging.info(\"Installing ado package %s from %s\", package, source)\n\n    if runtime.is_unix:\n        installer_cls = SOURCE_MAPPING[source]\n        install_args = [package, package_source_from] if source == \"net\" else [package]\n        install_kwargs = {\"confirm\": True}\n        if source == \"github\":\n            install_kwargs[\"allowed_repositories\"] = (\n                config.ADO_INSTALL_ALLOWED_GITHUB_REPOSITORIES\n            )\n        install_message = installer_cls(\n            runtime.stata_cli,\n            is_replace,\n            timeout=timeout,\n        ).install(*install_args, **install_kwargs)\n\n        return _finalize_install(\n            installer_cls,\n            package,\n            source,\n            install_message,\n            installer_cls.check_installed_from_msg(install_message),\n            config_file=config_file,\n        )\n\n    options = []\n    if is_replace:\n        options.append(\"replace\")\n    if source == \"net\":\n        options.append(f\"from({package_source_from})\")\n    option_text = f\", {' '.join(options)}\" if options else \"\"\n    command = f\"{source} install {package}{option_text}\"\n    dofile_path = write_dofile(command, config_file=config_file)\n    result = _stata_do(\n        dofile_path,\n        read_log_when_error=False,\n        config_file=config_file,\n        allow_package_management=True,\n    )\n    text_log_path = result.get(\"log_file_path\", {}).get(\"text\")\n    if not text_log_path:\n        return (\n            \"Installation State: False\\n\"\n            f\"Error: Stata did not produce an installation log. Details: {result}\"\n        )\n\n    log_content = read_log(\n        text_log_path,\n        output_format=\"core\",\n        config_file=config_file,\n    )\n    installer_cls = SOURCE_MAPPING[source]\n    is_installed = installer_cls.check_install(log_content)\n    install_message = f\"Installation State: {is_installed}\\n{log_content}\"\n    return _finalize_install(\n        installer_cls,\n        package,\n        source,\n        install_message,\n        is_installed,\n        config_file=config_file,\n    )\n\n\ndef _finalize_install(\n    installer_cls,\n    package: str,\n    source: str,\n    install_message: str,\n    is_installed: bool,\n    *,\n    config_file: str | Path | None,\n) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Refresh help after success or append consistent installation failure details.\"\"\"\n    if is_installed:\n        logging.info(\"Installed ado package %s from %s\", package, source)\n        _refresh_installed_package_help(\n            package,\n            source=source,\n            config_file=config_file,\n        )\n        return install_message\n\n    logging.error(\"Failed to install ado package %s from %s\", package, source)\n    error_summary = installer_cls.extract_error_summary(install_message)\n    install_message += (\n        f\"\\nError: Failed to install package '{package}' from source '{source}'. \"\n        f\"Details: {error_summary}\"\n    )\n    if source == \"github\":\n        install_message += (\n            \"\\nPlease check the GitHub repository URL, verify case sensitivity, \"\n            \"and ensure the github command is installed in Stata.\"\n        )\n    return install_message\n\n\ndef _refresh_installed_package_help(\n    package: str,\n    *,\n    source: str,\n    config_file: str | Path | None,\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Best-effort refresh the likely command help after a successful install.\"\"\"\n    help_command = package.rsplit(\"/\", maxsplit=1)[-1] if source == \"github\" else package\n    try:\n        stata_help(\n            help_command,\n            config_file=config_file,\n            replace=True,\n        )\n    except Exception as error:\n        logging.warning(\n            \"Installed package '%s', but could not refresh help for '%s': %s\",\n            package,\n            help_command,\n            error,\n        )\n"

     with debug_step(\n            \"get_data_info.runtime\",\n            tool=\"get_data_info\",\n            request_id=active_request_id,\n        ):\n            runtime = cache_enabled=data_info_config.is_cache,\n            duration_ms=elapsed_ms(stage_started_at),\n        )\n        auditor = DataPathAuditor(\n            working_dir=runtime.config.WORKING_DIR,\n allowed_url_domains=runtime.config.DATA_INFO_ALLOWED_URL_DOMAINS,\n            additional_allowed_dirs=getattr(\n                runtime.config,\n                \"ADDITIONAL_ALLOWED_DIRS\",\n                (),\n            ),\n        )\n\n        stage_started_at = time.perf_counter()\n        source_kind = \"url\" if auditor.is_url(data_path) else \"local\"\n        if source_kind == \"url\":\n attributes={\"source_kind\": source_kind, \"source_ref\": source_ref},\n            ):\n                validated_data = auditor.validate_url(data_path)\n            if not isinstance(validated_data,     log_event(\n                    logger,\n                    logging.WARNING,\n                    \"get_data_info.path.rejected\",\n                    active_request_id,\n logger,\n                    logging.INFO,\n                    \"get_data_info.request.completed\",\n                    active_request_id,\n                    duration_ms=elapsed_ms(started_at),\n log_event(\n                    logger,\n                    logging.WARNING,\n                    \"get_data_info.path.rejected\",\n                    active_request_id,\n                    duration_ms=elapsed_ms(stage_started_at),\n                    source_kind=source_kind,\n                    source_ref=source_ref,\n                )\n                log_event(\n                    logger,\n                    logging.INFO,\n                    \"get_data_info.request.completed\",\n                    active_request_id,\n                    duration_ms=elapsed_ms(started_at),\n logging.WARNING,\n                \"get_data_info.handler.unsupported\",\n                active_request_id,\n                suffix=data_extension,\n            )\n            log_event(\n                logger,\n                logging.INFO,\n                \"get_data_info.request.completed\",\n                active_request_id,\n                duration_ms=elapsed_ms(started_at),\n debug_step(\n            \"get_data_info.handler_initialization\",\n            tool=\"get_data_info\",\n            request_id=active_request_id,\n            attributes={\"suffix\": cache_dir=runtime.tmp_base_path,\n                head=resolved_head,\n                is_cache=data_info_config.is_cache,\n                metrics=data_info_config.metrics,\n request_id=active_request_id,\n            )\n        log_event(\n            logger,\n            logging.DEBUG,\n            \"get_data_info.handler.initialized\",\n            active_request_id,\n \"get_data_info.info_pipeline\",\n            tool=\"get_data_info\",\n            request_id=active_request_id,\n            attributes={\"suffix\": data_extension},\n        ):\n            data_summary = data_info.info\n        log_event(\n            logger,\n            logging.DEBUG,\n            \"get_data_info.info.completed\",\n            active_request_id,\n logger,\n            logging.DEBUG,\n            \"get_data_info.serialization.completed\",\n            active_request_id,\n            duration_ms=elapsed_ms(stage_started_at),\n \"get_data_info.request.completed\",\n            active_request_id,\n            duration_ms=elapsed_ms(started_at),\n            outcome=\"success\",\n            tool_result_utf8_bytes=result_utf8_bytes,\n        )\n        return result\n    except Exception as error:\n        log_event(\n            logger,\n            logging.ERROR,\n            \"get_data_info.request.failed\",\n            active_request_id,\n            duration_ms=elapsed_ms(started_at),\n            error_type=type(error).__name__,\n            source_ref=source_ref,\n )\n        if summary_started:\n            return f\"Failed to generate data summary for {resolved_data_path}: {error}\"\n        raise\n\n\ndef get_data_info(\n    data_path: str,\n    vars_list: \"\"\"Return descriptive statistics for a supported dataset.\"\"\"\n    return _get_data_info_impl(\n        data_path=data_path,\n        vars_list=vars_list,\n        encoding=encoding,\n        config_file=config_file,\n        head=head,\n        tool_context=tool_context,\n    )\n\n\ndef _record_data_path_rejection(\n    data_path: str,\n    rejection: str,\n    *,\n    source_kind: DofileSnapshot\nfrom .redaction import redact_value\nfrom .run_id import generate_run_id\n\nAuditTerminalEvent = Literal[\n    \"completed\",\n    \"failed\",\n    \"timeout\",\n    \"blocked\",\n    \"interrupted\",\n]\n\nSCHEMA_VERSION = 1\n_APPEND_LOCK = threading.Lock()\n_SNAPSHOT_LOCK = threading.Lock()\n_TOOL_NAME_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*$\")\n\n\nclass AuditStore:\n    \"\"\"Persist per-tool JSONL events and exact source snapshots.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, base_path: Path):\n        self.base_path = Path(base_path)\n        self.audit_path = self.base_path / \"audit\"\n        self.snapshot_path = self.base_path / \"snapshot\"\n        self.snapshot_objects_path = self.snapshot_path / \"objects\"\n\n    def start_run(\n        self,\n        tool: str,\n        source_reference: str,\n        input_payload: Mapping[str, Any],\n        interface: str = \"runtime\",\n        client: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,\n        protocol_version: str | None = None,\n        request_id: str | None = None,\n        timestamp_ns: int | None = None,\n    ) -> AuditRun:\n        \"\"\"Create a run and append its initial event before execution.\"\"\"\n        self._validate_tool_name(tool)\n        normalized_source = str(source_reference)\n        run_id, started_at, started_at_ns = generate_run_id(\n            tool,\n            normalized_source,\n            timestamp_ns=timestamp_ns,\n        )\n        run = AuditRun(\n            run_id=run_id,\n            tool=tool,\n            source_reference=normalized_source,\n            interface=interface,\n            started_at=started_at.isoformat(timespec=\"microseconds\"),\n            started_at_ns=started_at_ns,\n        )\n        event: dict[str, Any] = {\n            \"schema_version\": SCHEMA_VERSION,\n            \"run_id\": run.run_id,\n            \"event\": \"started\",\n            \"tool\": tool,\n            \"timestamp\": run.started_at,\n            \"interface\": interface,\n            \"source_reference\": redact_value(normalized_source),\n            \"input\": redact_value(dict(input_payload)),\n        }\n        if client is not None:\n            event[\"client\"] = redact_value(dict(client))\n        if protocol_version is not None:\n            event[\"protocol_version\"] = protocol_version\n        if request_id is not None:\n            event[\"request_id\"] = request_id\n        self._append_tool_event(tool, event)\n        return run\n\n    def finish_run(\n        self,\n        run: AuditRun,\n        event: AuditTerminalEvent,\n        *,\n        artifacts: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,\n        output: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,\n        error: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,\n        security_event_ids: list[str] | None = None,\n        executed: bool | None = None,\n        timestamp_ns: int | None = None,\n    ) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Append the terminal event without modifying prior records.\"\"\"\n        if event not in {\n            \"completed\",\n            \"failed\",\n            \"timeout\",\n            \"blocked\",\n            \"interrupted\",\n        }:\n            raise ValueError(f\"Unsupported terminal audit event: {event}\")\n        finished_at_ns = time.time_ns() if timestamp_ns is None else timestamp_ns\n        finished_at = datetime.fromtimestamp(\n            finished_at_ns / 1_000_000_000,\n            tz=timezone.utc,\n        )\n        event_payload: dict[str, Any] = {\n            \"schema_version\": (),\n) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Require a GitHub repository to be explicitly allowlisted.\"\"\"\n    normalized_repository = validate_ado_package_name(repository, source=\"github\")\n    normalized_allowlist = {\n        str(item).strip().lower()\n        for item in allowed_repositories\n        if str(item).strip()\n    }\n    if normalized_repository.lower() not in normalized_allowlist:\n        logger.warning(\n            \"[SECURITY VIOLATION] Rejected ado install request: %s\",\n            f\"GitHub repository '{normalized_repository}' is not allowlisted\",\n        )\n        raise PermissionError(\n            f\"GitHub repository '{normalized_repository}' is not allowlisted. \"\n            \"Configure SECURITY.ADO_INSTALL_ALLOWED_GITHUB_REPOSITORIES \"\n            \"before installing.\"\n        )\n    return normalized_repository\n\n\ndef validate_net_source_location(location: str | None) -> or UNSAFE_STATA_ARGUMENT_PATTERN.search(normalized_location)\n    ):\n        raise ValueError(\n            \"Invalid net package source location. All Rights Reserved\n#\n# @Author : Sepine Tam (谭淞)\n# @Email  : sepinetam@gmail.com\n# @File   : validator.py\n\n\"\"\"Security validation module for Stata dofiles.\n\nThis module provides the core validation logic for detecting dangerous\ncommands and patterns in Stata dofile code.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport logging\nimport re\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, field\nfrom typing import Any, List\n\nfrom ..utils.parse_dofile import (\n    ExpansionResult,\n    ParsedCommand,\n    expand_code_for_security,\n)\nfrom .blacklist import (\n    DANGEROUS_COMMANDS,\n    DANGEROUS_PATTERNS,\n    PACKAGE_MANAGEMENT_COMMANDS,\n    STATA_PREFIXES,\n)\nfrom .data_path_auditor import DataPathAuditor\n\nlogger = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n\nDIRECT_DATA_COMMANDS = {\n    \"use\",\n    \"import\",\n    \"insheet\",\n    \"infile\",\n    \"infix\",\n}\nUSING_DATA_COMMANDS = {\n    \"merge\",\n    \"merg\",\n    \"mer\",\n    \"append\",\n    \"appen\",\n    \"appe\",\n    \"app\",\n    \"ap\",\n    \"joinby\",\n    \"joinb\",\n}\nCONTEXT_MUTATION_COMMANDS = {\"cd\", \"chdir\"}\nPATH_LIKE_COMMANDS = (\n    DIRECT_DATA_COMMANDS\n    | USING_DATA_COMMANDS\n    | {\n        \"save\",\n        \"saveold\",\n        \"sysuse\",\n        \"webuse\",\n        \"export\",\n        \"outfile\",\n        \"outsheet\",\n        \"do\",\n        \"run\",\n        \"include\",\n        \"type\",\n        \"erase\",\n        \"rmdir\",\n        \"mkdir\",\n        \"copy\",\n    }\n)\nUNRESOLVED_MACRO_PATTERN = re.compile(\n    r\"`[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*'|\"\n    r\"`[=:]|\"\n    r\"\\$\\{[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*\\}|\"\n    r\"\\$[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*\"\n)\n\n# ============================================================================\n# Data Structures\n# ============================================================================\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass RiskItem:\n    \"\"\"Represents a single security risk item found in the code.\n\n    Attributes:\n        type: The type of risk (\"command\", \"pattern\", \"macro\", \"parse\",\n            \"context\", or \"data_path\")\n        content: The actual content that triggered the risk\n        line: Line number where the risk was found (1-indexed)\n    \"\"\"\n\n    type: str\n    content: str\n    line: int\n\n    def __str__(self) -> str:\n        \"\"\"Return string representation of the risk item.\"\"\"\n        return f\"Line {self.line}: {self.type} '{self.content}'\"\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass SecurityReport:\n    \"\"\"Security validation report for Stata dofile code.\n\n    Attributes:\n        is_safe: True if no dangerous items were found, False otherwise\n        dangerous_items: List of all dangerous items found in the code\n    \"\"\"\n\n    is_safe: bool\n    dangerous_items: List[RiskItem] = field(default_factory=list)\n\n    def __str__(self) -> str:\n        \"\"\"Return string representation of the security report.\"\"\"\n        if self.is_safe:\n            return \"✅ Code passed security validation\"\n\n        lines = [\"❌ Security validation failed. Found dangerous items:\"]\n        for item in self.dangerous_items:\n            lines.append(f\"  - {item}\")\n        return \"\\n\".join(lines)\n\n\n# ============================================================================\n# Core Validator\n# ============================================================================\n\n\nclass GuardValidator:\n    \"\"\"Validator for Stata dofile security.\n\n    This class validates Stata dofile code against a blacklist of\n    dangerous commands and patterns.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Initialize the validator with default blacklist.\"\"\"\n        self.dangerous_commands = DANGEROUS_COMMANDS\n        self.dangerous_patterns = DANGEROUS_PATTERNS\n        self.stata_prefixes = set(STATA_PREFIXES)\n\n    @staticmethod\n    def _strip_prefixes(line: str, prefixes: set) -> str:\n        \"\"\"Remove Stata command prefixes from a line.\n\n        Stata allows stacking prefixes (e.g., ``cap qui shell ...``),\n        so we loop until no more prefixes remain.\n\n        Args:\n            line: The code line to strip\n            prefixes: Set of prefix strings to remove\n\n        Returns:\n            The line with all leading prefixes removed\n        \"\"\"\n        cleaned_line = line\n        prefix_pattern = re.compile(r\"^\\s*(\\w+)\\s*:?\\s*\", re.IGNORECASE)\n        version_prefix_pattern = re.compile(\n            r\"^\\s*version\\s+\\d+(?:\\.\\d+)?\\s*:\\s*\",\n            re.IGNORECASE,\n        )\n        frame_prefix_pattern = re.compile(\n            r\"^\\s*frame\\s+[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*\\s*:\\s*\",\n            re.IGNORECASE,\n        )\n        while cleaned_line:\n            version_match = version_prefix_pattern.match(cleaned_line)\n            if version_match:\n                cleaned_line = cleaned_line[version_match.end():]\n                continue\n            frame_match = frame_prefix_pattern.match(cleaned_line)\n            if frame_match:\n                cleaned_line = cleaned_line[frame_match.end():]\n                continue\n            matched = prefix_pattern.match(cleaned_line)\n            if not matched or matched.group(1).lower() not in prefixes:\n                break\n            cleaned_line = cleaned_line[matched.end():]\n        return cleaned_line.strip()\n\n    @staticmethod\n    def _iter_executable_lines(lines: List[str]) -> List[tuple[int, str]]:\n        \"\"\"Return lines after removing Stata block comments.\"\"\"\n        executable_lines: List[tuple[int, str]] = []\n        in_block_comment = False\n\n        for line_num, line in enumerate(lines, start=1):\n            index = 0\n            cleaned_parts: List[str] = []\n\n            while index < len(line):\n                if in_block_comment:\n                    comment_end = line.find(\"*/\", index)\n                    if comment_end == -1:\n                        index = len(line)\n                    else:\n                        index = comment_end + 2\n                        in_block_comment = False\n                    continue\n\n                comment_start = line.find(\"/*\", index)\n                if comment_start == -1:\n                    cleaned_parts.append(line[index:])\n                    break\n\n                cleaned_parts.append(line[index:comment_start])\n                index = comment_start + 2\n                in_block_comment = True\n\n            executable_lines.append((line_num, \"\".join(cleaned_parts)))\n\n        return executable_lines\n\n    def validate(self, code: str, config: Any | None = None) -> SecurityReport:\n        \"\"\"Validate Stata dofile code for security risks.\n\n        Args:\n            code: The Stata dofile code to validate\n            config: Optional runtime config. When provided and\n                ``ENABLE_DATA_COMMAND_PATH_GUARD`` is True, data-loading\n                commands are audited for path/URL boundary violations.\n\n        Returns:\n            SecurityReport containing validation results\n        \"\"\"\n        dangerous_items: List[RiskItem] = []\n\n        original_executable_lines = self._iter_executable_lines(code.split(\"\\n\"))\n        dangerous_local_names = self._collect_dangerous_local_names(\n            original_executable_lines\n        )\n        for line_num, line in original_executable_lines:\n            stripped_line = line.strip()\n            if (\n                not stripped_line\n                or stripped_line.startswith(\"*\")\n                or stripped_line.startswith(\"//\")\n            ):\n                continue\n            cleaned_line = self._strip_prefixes(stripped_line, self.stata_prefixes)\n            dangerous_items.extend(\n                self._check_macro_expansion(\n                    cleaned_line, line_num, dangerous_local_names\n                )\n            )\n            dangerous_items.extend(\n                self._check_dangerous_patterns(cleaned_line, line_num)\n            )\n\n        expansion_result = expand_code_for_security(code)\n        if expansion_result.requires_global_fail_closed:\n            for diagnostic in expansion_result.diagnostics:\n                if not diagnostic.security_relevant or diagnostic.scope != \"global\":\n                    continue\n                dangerous_items.append(\n                    RiskItem(\n                        type=\"parse\",\n                        content=diagnostic.code,\n                        line=diagnostic.line,\n                    )\n                )\n\n        lines = expansion_result.expanded_code.split(\"\\n\")\n        executable_lines = self._iter_executable_lines(lines)\n\n        data_path_auditor = None\n        if config is not None and getattr(\n            config, \"ENABLE_DATA_COMMAND_PATH_GUARD\", False\n        ):\n            data_path_auditor = DataPathAuditor(\n                working_dir=config.WORKING_DIR,\n                strict_local_boundary=config.STRICT_DATA_INFO_LOCAL_BOUNDARY,\n                enable_url_guard=config.ENABLE_DATA_INFO_URL_GUARD,\n                allowed_url_domains=config.DATA_INFO_ALLOWED_URL_DOMAINS,\n                additional_allowed_dirs=getattr(\n                    config,\n                    \"ADDITIONAL_ALLOWED_DIRS\",\n                    (),\n                ),\n            )\n\n        for line_num, line in executable_lines:\n            origin_line_num = self._origin_line_for_expanded_line(\n                line_num,\n                expansion_result.line_map,\n            )\n            # Skip empty lines and comments\n            stripped_line = line.strip()\n            if (\n                not stripped_line\n                or stripped_line.startswith(\"*\")\n                or stripped_line.startswith(\"//\")\n            ):\n                continue\n\n            # Strip Stata prefixes (capture, quietly, etc.) before checking\n            cleaned_line = self._strip_prefixes(stripped_line, self.stata_prefixes)\n            if not cleaned_line:\n                continue\n\n            # Check for dangerous commands\n            command_items = self._check_dangerous_commands(\n                cleaned_line, origin_line_num\n            )\n            dangerous_items.extend(command_items)\n\n            # Check for dangerous patterns\n            pattern_items = self._check_dangerous_patterns(\n                cleaned_line, origin_line_num\n            )\n            dangerous_items.extend(pattern_items)\n\n        for command in expansion_result.commands:\n            dangerous_items.extend(\n                self._check_command_parse_diagnostics(\n                    command,\n                    expansion_result,\n                    data_path_guard_enabled=data_path_auditor is not None,\n                )\n            )\n\n        # Check data-loading command paths when the guard is enabled.\n        if data_path_auditor is not None:\n            for command in expansion_result.commands:\n                dangerous_items.extend(self._check_context_mutation_command(command))\n                dangerous_items.extend(\n                    self._check_data_command_path(command, data_path_auditor)\n                )\n\n        # Generate report\n        is_safe = len(dangerous_items) == 0\n        if not is_safe:\n            item_summary = \", \".join(\n                f\"line {item.line}:{item.type}\" for item in dangerous_items\n            )\n            logger.warning(\n                \"[SECURITY VIOLATION] Guard blocked dangerous dofile; items=[%s]\",\n                item_summary,\n            )\n        else:\n            logger.debug(\"Guard validation passed with no dangerous items\")\n        return SecurityReport(is_safe=is_safe, dangerous_items=dangerous_items)\n\n    @staticmethod\n    def _origin_line_for_expanded_line(\n        expanded_line_num: int,\n        line_map: dict[int, list[int]],\n    ) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Return the first original source line for an expanded line.\"\"\"\n        origins = line_map.get(expanded_line_num)\n        if origins:\n            return origins[0]\n        return expanded_line_num\n\n    def _collect_dangerous_local_names(self, lines: List[tuple[int, str]]) -> set[str]:\n        \"\"\"Collect macro names whose values are dangerous commands.\"\"\"\n        dangerous_names: set[str] = set()\n        macro_pattern = re.compile(\n            r\"^\\s*(?:local|global)\\s+(\\w+)\\s+(.+)$\", re.IGNORECASE\n        )\n\n        for _line_num, line in lines:\n            stripped_line = line.strip()\n            if (\n                not stripped_line\n                or stripped_line.startswith(\"*\")\n                or stripped_line.startswith(\"//\")\n            ):\n                continue\n\n            cleaned_line = self._strip_prefixes(stripped_line, self.stata_prefixes)\n            matched = macro_pattern.search(cleaned_line)\n            if not matched:\n                continue\n\n            local_name, local_value = matched.group(1), self._strip_macro_value_quotes(\n                matched.group(2)\n            )\n            first_value_token = (\n                self._normalize_command_token(local_value.split()[0])\n                if local_value.split()\n                else \"\"\n            )\n            if first_value_token in self.dangerous_commands:\n                dangerous_names.add(local_name)\n\n        return dangerous_names\n\n    @staticmethod\n    def _strip_macro_value_quotes(value: str) -> str:\n        \"\"\"Remove Stata macro value quotes, including compound quotes.\"\"\"\n        stripped_value = value.strip()\n        if (\n            len(stripped_value) >= 4\n            and stripped_value.startswith('`\"')\n            and stripped_value.endswith(\"\\\"'\")\n        ):\n            return stripped_value[2:-2]\n        if (\n            len(stripped_value) >= 2\n            and stripped_value[0] == stripped_value[-1]\n            and stripped_value[0] in {'\"', \"'\"}\n        ):\n            return stripped_value[1:-1]\n        return stripped_value\n\n    @staticmethod\n    def _check_macro_expansion(\n        line: str, line_num: int, dangerous_local_names: set[str]\n    ) -> List[RiskItem]:\n        \"\"\"Check whether a line expands a dangerous macro.\"\"\"\n        items: List[RiskItem] = []\n        for local_name in dangerous_local_names:\n            if re.search(rf\"(?<!\\w)`{re.escape(local_name)}'(?!\\w)\", line):\n                macro_token = f\"`{local_name}'\"\n                items.append(RiskItem(type=\"macro\", content=macro_token, line=line_num))\n            if re.search(rf\"(?<!\\w)\\${re.escape(local_name)}(?!\\w)\", line):\n                macro_token = f\"${local_name}\"\n                items.append(RiskItem(type=\"macro\", content=macro_token, line=line_num))\n            if re.search(rf\"(?<!\\w)\\$\\{{{re.escape(local_name)}\\}}(?!\\w)\", line):\n                macro_token = f\"${local_name}\"\n                items.append(RiskItem(type=\"macro\", content=macro_token, line=line_num))\n        return items\n\n    def _check_command_parse_diagnostics(\n        self,\n        command: ParsedCommand,\n        expansion_result: ExpansionResult,\n        data_path_guard_enabled: bool,\n    ) -> List[RiskItem]:\n        \"\"\"Fail closed on line-scoped parser uncertainty for sensitive commands.\"\"\"\n        diagnostics = [\n            diagnostic\n            for diagnostic in expansion_result.diagnostics_on(command)\n            if diagnostic.security_relevant and diagnostic.scope == \"line\"\n        ]\n        if not diagnostics:\n            return []\n\n        if not self._command_requires_line_fail_closed(\n            command,\n            data_path_guard_enabled=data_path_guard_enabled,\n        ):\n            return []\n\n        line_num = self._command_origin_line(command)\n        return [\n            RiskItem(\n                type=\"parse\",\n                content=diagnostic.code,\n                line=diagnostic.line or line_num,\n            )\n            for diagnostic in diagnostics\n        ]\n\n    def _command_requires_line_fail_closed(\n        self,\n        command: ParsedCommand,\n        data_path_guard_enabled: bool,\n    ) -> bool:\n        \"\"\"Return True when parser uncertainty on this command is security-sensitive.\"\"\"\n        if UNRESOLVED_MACRO_PATTERN.search(command.name):\n            return True\n        if command.name in self.dangerous_commands:\n            return True\n        if command.text.startswith(\"!\"):\n            return True\n        if data_path_guard_enabled and (\n            command.name in PATH_LIKE_COMMANDS\n            or command.name in CONTEXT_MUTATION_COMMANDS\n        ):\n            return True\n        return False\n\n    @staticmethod\n    def _check_context_mutation_command(command: ParsedCommand) -> List[RiskItem]:\n        \"\"\"Reject commands that make later relative path auditing unreliable.\"\"\"\n        if command.name not in CONTEXT_MUTATION_COMMANDS:\n            return []\n        line_num = GuardValidator._command_origin_line(command)\n        logger.warning(\n            \"[SECURITY VIOLATION] Guard blocked context-mutating command: \"\n            \"command='%s', line=%d\",\n            command.name,\n            line_num,\n        )\n        return [RiskItem(type=\"context\", content=command.name, line=line_num)]\n\n    def _check_dangerous_commands(self, line: str, line_num: int) -> List[RiskItem]:\n        \"\"\"Check if a line contains dangerous commands.\n\n        Args:\n            line: The code line to check\n            line_num: Line number\n\n        Returns:\n            List of RiskItem objects found\n        \"\"\"\n        items: List[RiskItem] = []\n\n        # Get the first word (command)\n        first_word = (\n            self._normalize_command_token(line.split()[0]) if line.split() else \"\"\n        )\n\n        if first_word in self.dangerous_commands:\n            items.append(RiskItem(type=\"command\", content=first_word, line=line_num))\n\n        # Special check for \"!\" which is a prefix\n        if line.startswith(\"!\"):\n            items.append(RiskItem(type=\"command\", content=\"!\", line=line_num))\n\n        return items\n\n    @staticmethod\n    def _normalize_command_token(token: str) -> str:\n        \"\"\"Normalize command-position punctuation before blacklist matching.\"\"\"\n        return token.lower().rstrip(\",:\")\n\n    def _check_dangerous_patterns(self, line: str, line_num: int) -> List[RiskItem]:\n        \"\"\"Check if a line matches dangerous patterns.\n\n        Args:\n            line: The code line to check\n            line_num: Line number\n\n All Rights Reserved\n#\n# @Author : Sepine Tam (谭淞)\n# @Email  : sepinetam@gmail.com\n# @File   : ram_monitor.py\n\n\"\"\"\nNotes:\n    This monitor feature was coded by Claude Code with GLM-4.7.\n\n    By default, monitoring is disabled. If you want to control the maximum\n    performance on your device, we suggest you review the code carefully\n    before using it in production.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport logging\nimport threading\nfrom typing import Optional\n\nimport psutil\n\nfrom ..core.types import RAMLimitExceededError\nfrom .base import MonitorBase\n\n\nclass RAMMonitor(MonitorBase):\n    \"\"\"Monitor subprocess RAM usage during Stata execution.\n\n    This monitor runs in a separate thread and checks the RAM usage of the\n    Stata process at regular intervals. If the RAM usage exceeds the configured\n    limit, it will kill the process and raise RAMLimitExceededError.\n\n    Attributes:\n        max_ram_mb: Maximum RAM allowed in MB (None = no limit)\n\n    Example:\n        >>> # Create monitor instance with configuration\n        >>> monitor = RAMMonitor(max_ram_mb=8192)\n        >>> # Start monitoring (called by StataDo)\n        >>> monitor.start(process)\n        >>> # ... process runs ...\n        >>> # Stop monitoring (called by StataDo)\n        >>> monitor.stop()\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, max_ram_mb: Optional[int] = None):\n        \"\"\"\n        Initialize the RAM monitor.\n\n        Args:\n            max_ram_mb: Maximum RAM allowed in MB. If None, no monitoring is done.\n        \"\"\"\n        self.max_ram_mb = max_ram_mb\n        self.process = None\n        self._stop_event = threading.Event()\n        self._monitor_thread: Optional[threading.Thread] = None\n        self._exceeded_with_error: Optional[RAMLimitExceededError] = None\n\n    def start(self, process) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Start monitoring the given process.\n\n        Args:\n            process: subprocess.Popen object to monitor\n        \"\"\"\n        self.process = process\n\n        if self.max_ram_mb is None:\n            # No limit configured, don't start monitoring\n            logging.debug(\"No RAM limit configured, skipping monitoring\")\n            return\n\n        def monitor_loop():\n            \"\"\"Main monitoring loop that runs in a separate thread.\"\"\"\n            while not self._stop_event.is_set():\n                # Check if process is still running\n                if self.process.poll() is not None:\n                    # Process has finished\n                    logging.debug(f\"Process (PID: {self.process.pid}) has finished\")\n                    break\n\n                # Check RAM usage\n                try:\n                    # Get the process object\n                    psutil_process = psutil.Process(self.process.pid)\n\n                    # Get RAM usage in MB (RSS - Resident Set Size)\n                    ram_mb = psutil_process.memory_info().rss / 1024 / 1024\n\n                    # Check if exceeded\n                    if ram_mb > self.max_ram_mb:\n                        # Store the exception to be raised later\n                        self._exceeded_with_error = RAMLimitExceededError(\n                            ram_used_mb=ram_mb,\n                            ram_limit_mb=self.max_ram_mb\n                        )\n\n                        logging.warning(\n                            f\"RAM limit exceeded: {ram_mb:.0f}MB > {self.max_ram_mb}MB. \"\n                            f\"Killing Stata process (PID: {self.process.pid})\"\n                        )\n\n                        # Kill the process\n                        self.process.kill()\n                        break\n\n                except (psutil.NoSuchProcess, psutil.AccessDenied) as e:\n                    # Process may have finished or we don't have access\n                    logging.debug(f\"Could not monitor process RAM: {e}\")\n                    break\n                except Exception as e:\n                    logging.error(f\"Unexpected error monitoring process RAM: {e}\")\n                    break\n\n                # Wait before next check (0.5 seconds)\n                self._stop_event.wait(0.5)\n\n        # Start daemon thread (will be killed when main thread exits)\n        self._monitor_thread = threading.Thread(target=monitor_loop, daemon=True)\n        self._monitor_thread.start()\n\n        logging.info(\n            f\"Started RAM monitoring for Stata process (PID: {self.process.pid}), \"\n            f\"limit: {self.max_ram_mb}MB\"\n        )\n\n    def stop(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Stop monitoring and check if RAM limit was exceeded.\n\n        Raises:\n            RAMLimitExceededError: If RAM limit was exceeded during monitoring\n        \"\"\"\n        self._stop_event.set()\n        if self._monitor_thread and self._monitor_thread.is_alive():\n            self._monitor_thread.join(timeout=1.0)\n        logging.debug(\"RAM monitor stopped\")\n\n        # If RAM limit was exceeded, raise the exception\n        if self._exceeded_with_error:\n            raise self._exceeded_with_error\n"

All Rights Reserved\n#\n# @Author : Sepine Tam (谭淞)\n# @Email  : sepinetam@gmail.com\n# @File   : base.py\n\nimport logging\nfrom abc import ABC, abstractmethod\n\nfrom ...stata_controller import StataController\n\nlogger = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n\n\nclass AdoInstallBase(ABC):\n    def __init__(self,\n                 stata_cli,\n                 is_replace: bool = False,\n                 timeout: int = 300):\n        self.stata_cli = stata_cli\n        self.is_replace = is_replace\n        self.timeout = timeout\n        self.__post_initialization()\n\n    def __post_initialization(self):\n        \"\"\"\n        Post-initialization hook for subclasses to override.\n\n        This method is called automatically after __init__ completes.\n        Subclasses can override this method to perform additional initialization\n        without having to override the entire __init__ method.\n\n        Examples:\n            >>> class MyInstaller(AdoInstallBase):\n            ...     def __post_initialization(self):\n            ...         self.github_mirror = \"https://github.com\"  # Fake var\n            ...\n            ...     def install(self, package: str):\n            ...         ...\n        \"\"\"\n        pass\n\n    @property\n    def controller(self) -> StataController:\n        return StataController(self.stata_cli, timeout=self.timeout)\n\n    @property\n    def REPLACE_MESSAGE(self) -> str:\n        if self.is_replace:\n            return \", replace\"\n        else:\n            return \"\"\n\n    @abstractmethod\n    def install(self, package: str) -> str: pass\n\n    @staticmethod\n    @abstractmethod\n    def check_install(message: str) -> bool:\n        ...\n\n    @staticmethod\n    def check_installed_from_msg(msg: str) -> bool:\n        state_with_prompt = msg.split(\"\\n\")[0]\n        state_str = state_with_prompt.split(\":\")[-1].strip().lower()\n        return state_str in (\"true\", \"1\", \"yes\")\n\n    def _run_install_command(self, install_command: str, *, source: str, package: str) -> str:\n        \"\"\"Run an install command in Stata with lifecycle audit logging.\n\n        The raw command (which may embed a source URL) is intentionally not\n        logged; only the package name and source are recorded.\n        \"\"\"\n        logger.info(\"Running Stata install command for package %s (source=%s)\", package, source)\n        try:\n            runner_result = self.controller.run(install_command)\n        except Exception as error:\n            logger.error(\"Stata install command failed for package %s (source=%s): %s\", package, source, error)\n            raise\n        return runner_result\n\n    def _install_msg_template(self, runner_result: str) -> str:\n        \"\"\"Mark a completed interactive install successful.\n\n        StataController raises for Stata return-code errors, timeouts, and\n        terminated sessions. Reaching this point therefore represents a\n        successful Unix installation command.\n        \"\"\"\n        return \"Installation State: True\\n\" + runner_result\n\n    @staticmethod\n    def extract_error_summary(message: str) -> str:\n        lines = [line.strip() for line in str(message).splitlines() if line.strip()]\n        if not lines:\n            return \"Unknown installation failure.\"\n\n        error_keywords = (\n            \"r(\",\n            \"not found\",\n            \"could not\",\n            \"failed\",\n            \"error\",\n            \"invalid\",\n            \"unable\",\n            \"permission denied\",\n            \"connection\",\n            \"timed out\",\n        )\n        matched_lines = [\n            line for line in lines\n            if any(keyword in line.lower() for keyword in error_keywords)\n        ]\n\n        if matched_lines:\n            return \" | \".join(matched_lines[-3:])\n        return lines[-1]\n"

Use a set of patterns to match various prompt scenarios\n        patterns = [\n            r\"\\r\\n\\. \",  # Standard prompt\n            r\"\\r\\n: \",  # Continuation prompt\n            r\"\\r\\n--more--\",  # More content prompt\n            r\"r\\(\\d+\\);\",  # Error prompt\n            pexpect.TIMEOUT,  # Timeout\n            pexpect.EOF,  # End of program\n        ]\n\n        index = self.child.expect(patterns, timeout=timeout)\n\n        # Continue waiting until standard prompt appears\n            try:\n                self.child.expect(r\"\\r\\n\\. \", timeout=5)\n            except pexpect.TIMEOUT:\n                pass  # Ignore timeout and return error index\n            return index\n        elif index == 4:  # Timeout\n            # Try sending a newline to trigger the prompt\n            self.child.sendline(\"\")\n            try:\n                self.child.expect([r\"\\r\\n\\. \", pexpect.TIMEOUT], timeout=5)\n            except pexpect.TIMEOUT:\n                pass\n            return index\n\n        return index\n\n    def run(self, command, timeout=None):\n        \"\"\"\n        Execute a Stata command and wait for completion.\n\n        Args:\n            command (str): The Stata command to execute.\n            timeout (int, optional): Timeout for this command.\n\n        Returns:\n            str: The output of the command execution.\n\n        Raises:\n            RuntimeError: If the command times out or other errors occur.\n        \"\"\"\n        if timeout is None:\n            timeout = self.timeout\n\n        self._last_error_code = None\n        self._last_error_output = None\n\n        # Send the command\n        self.child.sendline(command)\n\n        # Wait for the command to complete\n        result = self._expect_prompt(timeout)\n\n        # Capture the output\n        output = (\n            self._last_error_output\n            if result == 3 and self._last_error_output is not None\n            else self.child.before.strip()\n        )\n\n        # Check for errors\n        if result == 3:  # Error prompt index\n            if self._last_error_code is not None:\n                raise RuntimeError(\n                    f\"Stata error r({self._last_error_code}): {output}\"\n                )\n            raise RuntimeError(f\"Stata command failed: {output}\")\n        elif result == 4:  # Timeout\n            raise RuntimeError(f\"Command timed out (> {timeout}s): {command}\")\n        elif result == 5:  # EOF\n            raise RuntimeError(\n                f\"Stata session terminated unexpectedly: {output}\")\n\n        return output\n\n    def run_with_retry(self, command, max_retries=3, timeout=None):\n        \"\"\"\n        Execute a command with a retry mechanism.\n\n        Args:\n            command (str): The Stata command to execute.\n            max_retries (int): Maximum number of retry attempts.\n            timeout (int, optional): Timeout for this command.\n\n        Returns:\n            str: The output of the command execution.\n\n        Raises:\n            RuntimeError: If all retry attempts fail.\n        \"\"\"\n        retries = 0\n        last_error = None\n\n        while retries < max_retries:\n            try:\n                return self.run(command, timeout)\n            except RuntimeError as e:\n                last_error = e\n                retries += 1\n                # Execute command with retry\n        use_data = temp_stata_session.run_with_retry(f\"use {url}, clear\")\n        if \"not found\" in use_data or \"server reported server error\" in use_data:\n            print(\"Stata data not found.
